newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS - De Beers looks to explore W.Australia.
newsitem.headline: RTRS - De Beers looks to explore W.Australia.

text.p: South Africa's De Beers Consolidated Mines said on Wednesday future diamond prospecting work in Australia would focus on less explored areas, including the Yilgarn region of Western Australia state.

"We feel diamond exploration in Western Australia is far from mature and will be spending more money on these hard to get at areas," Joe Joyce, chief geologist for Stockdale Prospecting Ltd, the wholly-owned Australian exploration arm of De Beers told reporters after addressing the Paydirt diamond conference here.
Joyce said in the past, exploration work by Stockdale and other companies concentrated on more accessible Kimberley region in the north of the state.
"The north is more explored than the south," Joyce said. "I can see a long-term trend where more of our friends will come this way."
The world's single largest diamond mine, the Argyle mine, is located in the Kimberely region. It is 60 percent owned by RTZ Corp Plc-CRA Ltd and 40 percent by Ashton Mining Ltd.
Stockdale plans to maintain its annual A$10 million exploration budget in the current year, with about half earmarked for the Yilgarn block and Pilbara region, north of Kalgoorlie, Joyce said.
Astro Mining NL said on Tuesday said it would spend around A$5 million on research and exploration concentrating on the Yilgarn over the next three years.
Stockdale have discovered 70 kimberlite pipes, suggesting the presence of diamonds, in the last 20 years.
But none of the finds met Stockdale's criteria for development of a three million carat a year deposit, averaging US$75 a carat over a minimum 10-year mine life, Joyce said.

Joyce said any future joint ventures with Australian companies would first need to meet De Beers requirements for control of operations and willingness to sell through the De Beers-controlled Central Selling Organisation diamond cooperative.
